page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-96 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 192 GB of RAM, providing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 82682.91 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21998.0. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in encryption tests and image processing. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 298.66 GB/sec for large block read-only operations, though overall memory performance registers in the average tier.

This instance delivers high throughput for network and text-heavy operations, achieving 129.97 GB/sec in static web serving and 105.66 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It is highly efficient for compute-dense workloads such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing. The lack of local storage and GPUs makes it a specialized choice for stateless compute tasks, high-performance web serving, and parallel processing workloads.
